sentences.t: This is my desk, and it lives in the corner of a forty square metre apartment, so every single thing on it has to earn its spot.
I've changed a lot since last year's video, so let's go through all of it.
Starting with the desk itself, it's a cheap standing frame with a butcher block top I cut down to a hundred and twenty centimetres.
Anything bigger and I can't open the window behind me, which I found out the hard way.
I oiled the top myself, three coats, and it's holding up really well, even with coffee spills.
The frame is a dual motor one, and honestly the second motor is the upgrade, it doesn't wobble at standing height anymore.
Next, the monitor.
This is a thirty-four inch ultrawide, and the trick that made this whole setup work is the monitor arm.
Because it's on an arm, I can push the screen all the way back against the wall, and suddenly I've got this whole strip of desk in front of the keyboard.
That's where my notebook lives, and my coffee, and usually my cat.
Okay, before I get into the cables, which are honestly the part I'm most proud of, let me tell you about today's sponsor, 1Password.
I switched to 1Password about a year ago after realizing I was using the same three passwords for everything, which, yeah, not great.
It generates a strong password for every site, saves it, and fills it in for you on your laptop, your phone, and your browser.
It also warns you when one of your accounts shows up in a data breach, so you know exactly what to change.
And for this setup specifically, I love that I can unlock it with the fingerprint reader on my keyboard instead of typing a master password twenty times a day.
You can try 1Password free for fourteen days at 1password.com slash deskhaus.
That's 1password.com slash deskhaus, and the link is down in the description.
Okay, cables.
Underneath the desk there's a metal cable tray screwed into the top, and everything runs into that.
The power strip is stuck to the bottom of the tray with heavy-duty velcro, so it moves with the desk when I stand up.
That's the important bit with a standing desk, if anything is tied to the wall, it's going to yank out when you raise it.
There's exactly one cable going down to the floor, and it runs inside this cheap spine thing that cost me about twelve dollars.
Everything on top goes through one dock, so the laptop gets one cable and that's it.
Last thing, lighting, and this is the change that actually made the biggest difference to how I feel.
My window faces east, so by about two in the afternoon the room goes kind of gray and gloomy.
I added a light bar on top of the monitor, which lights the desk without glaring on the screen.
And behind the monitor there's an LED strip bounced off the wall, which sounds like a gamer thing, but at a warm white it just makes the room feel bigger.
I genuinely used to get headaches by four, and since the lighting change, I just don't.
So that's the setup, small, but it finally works for me.
Before you go, thanks again to 1Password for sponsoring this video, you can try it free for fourteen days at 1password.com slash deskhaus.
